newsitem.title: USA: Fannie, Freddie hike loan limits.
newsitem.headline: Fannie, Freddie hike loan limits.

text.p: Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac Wednesday said they will increase their single-family mortgage loan limit to $214,600 for 1997.
Limits for multi-unit loans also will be increased for 1997 as follows: two-family loans to $274,550; three-family loans to $331,850; and four-family loans to $412,450.
The maximum amount for one-to-four family mortgages in Alaska, Hawaii, and the U.S. Virgin Islands is 50 percent higher than the limits for the rest of the country.

The new limit is consistent with the increase in the Federal Housing Finance Board's national average home prices, after accounting for the decline in the average home prices that occurred between Oct 1992 and October 1993.
The limit establishes a ceiling for loans that the two firms can purchase. The ceiling is currently $207,000.

The housing finance board reported that the national average one-family housed purchased in October cost $156,800. This compared with $144,600 in 1995, $141,900 in 1994, 144,000 in 1993 and $148,400 in 1992.
The decision to take past home price index declines into account when setting next year's loan limit follows Congressional pressure.

Legislation introduced in the House would have required past losses to taken into account before the loan limit could be increased. The bill was not taken up by Congress before it adjourned, but its sponsors plan to proceed with it next year.
